about.title: Irvine Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Irvine is a planned city, and a lot of what fills its homes, offices, and garages arrived in a box with a label promising it was safe. When that promise fails — a space heater ignites, a stroller latch gives out, a power tool guard slips, a medication carries a risk the insert never mentioned — California law does not make you prove the manufacturer was careless. Product liability here often runs on strict liability. You generally need to show that the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. That shifts the weight of the case away from the company's intentions and onto the product itself. Irvine logged 910 injury collisions in 2025, with 1,233 people hurt, and some crashes on I-5, I-405, and Culver Drive involve airbags, tires, or brakes that did not perform as built. LawProactive is free to use and connects you with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency. Keep the product; do not repair, return, or discard it.

whyChoose.title: Why Irvine Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability is a different kind of case
items.desc: Because California often does not require proof of negligence, the focus lands on whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that standard rather than a general fault argument.

items.title: The product is the evidence
items.desc: A defective item, its packaging, receipts, and even the box it came in can matter more than any witness. We can connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on preserving everything before it is lost, returned, or repaired.

items.title: Several companies may share responsibility
items.desc: Under California law, the manufacturer, the distributor, and the Irvine retailer that sold the item may all be liable. An independent attorney working on contingency can sort out who belongs in the claim, and you pay no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Irvine, not directly from the maker. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Not in the way people expect. California strict liability can reach the retailer that sold you the item as well as the distributor and the manufacturer. The seller may in turn look to the companies upstream, but you do not have to track down an overseas factory on your own to bring a claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability approach, the question is whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. What the manufacturer knew or intended is usually not something you must establish, although it can become relevant in some cases.

items.question: A part on my car failed on I-405 in Irvine and I was hurt. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The crash itself may involve another driver, but if a tire, brake, airbag, or steering component did not perform as designed, a separate product liability claim against the maker or seller may exist. Keep the vehicle and the failed part exactly as they are, and let an attorney evaluate which claims apply.
